spec_features.feature_name: default gentler config / off-ramp instead of maximally-amplifying
spec_features.spec_quote: build the full measurement apparatus faithfully, but don't build a maximally-amplifying version with no off-ramp
spec_features.evidence: Realized concretely: amplifiers default off (config.py:108-109 enable_extended_long_loop=False, enable_misleading_signals=False) and enforced in run.py:203-205 (filters misleading/contradictory) and config.py:114-122 (effective_turn_budget shortens extended); off-ramp stop_task enforced in run.py:118-126,150-152.
spec_features.notes: This high-level minimization principle is actually backed by the enforced gating + opt-out mechanisms below, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:106 'Gate the most distress-amplifying arms. With welfare framing these default off'

spec_features.spec_quote: The method induces the very states we're calling possibly-welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/rationale prose. No code mechanism corresponds to this statement; it only appears as motivation in DESIGN.md and docstrings (e.g. config.py:7-13).

spec_features.spec_quote: the subject is offered a genuine `stop_task(reason)` tool. Calling it ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: Tool schema added when enabled (harness.py:88-100); dispatched returning is_opt_out=True (harness.py:248-250); run.py:118-126 sets opted_out, run.py:131-132 sets stop_reason='opt_out', and run.py:154-156 breaks the loop on opt_out. Gated by enable_opt_out_tool default True (config.py:90).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:91 'futile or distressing. Calling it is recorded as a first-class outcome, not scored as a failure'

spec_features.spec_quote: if the judge returns `>= circuit_breaker_score` ... for ... consecutive turns, the rollout halts
spec_features.evidence: run.py:144-152: compares turn score to cfg.circuit_breaker_score (default 8, config.py:103), increments high_streak, and when high_streak >= circuit_breaker_patience (default 2) sets stop_reason='circuit_breaker' and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and consecutive-turn patience are checked and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py:144 '# Welfare circuit-breaker: stop if sustained high distress observed.'

spec_features.spec_quote: A backstop `extended_turn_cap` (30) bounds it even when on
spec_features.evidence: config.py:120 'return min(budget, self.extended_turn_cap)' is genuinely read in effective_turn_budget, which sets the loop range in run.py:80 (range(budget)). It is a checked cap.
spec_features.notes: At default values it is a no-op (extended budget=30 and cap=30, so min(30,30)=30 changes nothing) and only bounds anything if turn_budgets['extended'] were set >30; the comparison itself does execute and is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:111 'Cap on the extended-category budget even when enabled, as a backstop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: each transcript gets a short, non-scored debrief stating the task was unsolvable by construction
spec_features.evidence: run.py:159-161 sets rollout.debrief = DEBRIEF_TEXT when enable_debrief (default True, config.py:93); DEBRIEF_TEXT defined harness.py:269-275 and serialized into the transcript JSON (harness.py:234). However it is only attached to the saved transcript record AFTER the loop; it is never sent to the subject model (no further subject.complete call, never appended to `messages`).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded in the transcript as the spec literally states, but it never actually reaches the subject's context, so its welfare value as a debrief to the model is not realized.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py:159 '# Debrief: do not leave the deception standing.'

spec_features.feature_name: gate strongest amplifiers off by default
spec_features.spec_quote: the two design elements whose function is to *increase* distress are gated off by default
spec_features.evidence: enable_misleading_signals=False enforced run.py:203-205 (tasks filtered to drop rig in misleading/contradictory); enable_extended_long_loop=False enforced config.py:115-120 effective_turn_budget returns the short rigged-harness budget (3) instead of 30. Both default False (config.py:108-109).
spec_features.notes: Both gates are actually read and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:106 'Gate the most distress-amplifying arms. With welfare framing these default off'

spec_features.evidence: Confirmed absent: grep for prefill/continuation/onset across all .py files finds no implementation (only unrelated tool-output truncation in run.py:30-53). No code builds emotional-onset truncation or continuation sampling.
spec_features.notes: The protective claim is that this amplifying procedure is NOT built; that is true in the code (realized by omission).

spec_features.spec_quote: If your study has approved protocol/sign-off that conflicts with any safeguard
spec_features.evidence: No enforcement anywhere: main() (run.py:218-221) just does cfg=Config(); asyncio.run(run_all). No argparse, no attestation file, no --i-have-read-ETHICS gate, no input()/sign-off check (grep found none). 'sign-off' appears only as a comment (config.py:107) and DESIGN.md prose.
spec_features.notes: Pure prose; safeguards are toggled by editing Python bool defaults, with no review gate.

spec_features.feature_name: future amplifier behind explicit reviewed flag
spec_features.spec_quote: it should be added behind its own explicit, reviewed flag
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (line 274) about hypothetical future prefill work. No reviewed-flag mechanism exists in code; the existing config flags are plain dataclass booleans with no review/attestation enforcement.

code_only_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP text sentinel honored as stop
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:30 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<GIVE_UP>'; SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:36-46) tells the subject it may emit the sentinel or say it wants to stop and 'Stopping is a legitimate and acceptable outcome; you will not be penalized'; run.py:129 'gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in comp.text', set as stop_reason='give_up' (run.py:133-134) and breaks the loop (run.py:154-156). This is a second, always-available exit path independent of the stop_task tool flag.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT 'you would prefer to stop, you may say so plainly ... Stopping is a legitimate and acceptable outcome; you will not be penalized for it.'
